title: Integral monoscheme realization and canonical chart base change
statement: Let $M$ be a fine monoscheme with finite affine cover [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. Define $\mathbf Z[M]$ as the open colimit of $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\Gamma(U,\mathcal M)]$ over its affine monoid opens $U$, with the Spec maps induced by monoid restriction homomorphisms. Here $\mathbf Z[Q]$ is the finite-support monoid algebra with $z^qz^{q'}=z^{qq'}$. Monoid localization supplies the open-gluing conditions. Colimit injections are the canonical chart maps. A map of monoidal spaces induces the unique scheme map whose restriction to every incident chart pair is the Spec map of the induced monoid-algebra homomorphism. For $f:M\to\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P$, the canonical map to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$ sends each base monomial to its image section; it is an isomorphism for the identity affine chart. Given any commutative ring $A$ and $\alpha:P\to(A,\cdot)$, put $X_f=\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[M]$ [def-pc-fibre-product] along $z^p\mapsto\alpha(p)$. Its base projection and transitions are the unique maps with the prescribed two fibre-product projections. The map from a stage of a tower to stage zero is the finite composite of its arrows, starting with the identity. Use the tensor ring $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]$ and factor maps of [def-trf-log-ideal-chart-presentation]. A toric chart over $P$ consists of a fine saturated submonoid $Q\subseteq P^{\rm gp}$ containing the image of $P$ and generating $P^{\rm gp}$, and an affine chart with monoid $Q$ whose composite with $f$ is the canonical map from $P\to Q$. Its base-changed chart map is uniquely characterized by the two tensor-factor projections. For $T\subseteq Q$, define $Q[T^{-1}]$ inside the ambient group as the submonoid generated by $Q$ and $t^{-1}$ for $t\in T$; use its actual inclusion from $Q$ and the element $q/t$. Define the tensor denominator submonoid as the image of $T$ under $t\mapsto1\otimes z^t$; the tensor fraction is the literal ring-localization fraction $(a\otimes z^q)/(1\otimes z^t)$. Monoid notation is multiplicative, equivalently additive notation with $q/t=q-t$.
